memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "After that, he took the fat, the fat tail, all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, both kidneys and their fat and the right thigh. And from the basket of bread made without yeast, which was before the LORD, he took one thick loaf, one thick loaf with olive oil mixed in, and one thin loaf, and he put these on the fat portions and on the right thigh." - Lev 8:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Meat and bread together. The richest portions of the animal, and three loaves from the basket.

This is the ordination offering, and it draws on everything that has come before. There are elements of the fellowship offering here, and elements of the grain offering. The whole sacrificial vocabulary of chapters 1–7 is gathered into one act.

That is fitting. A calling to serve God is not one thing. It requires atonement, dedication, thanksgiving, and fellowship all at once.

Notice the bread specifically: bread that was before the LORD. It had been sitting in God's presence. Now it is placed in the hands of the men being set apart.

What God gives His servants to carry, He first keeps in His own presence.

That is a good pattern for anyone who speaks for God — teachers, parents, preachers, friends offering counsel. What you hand to others should first have been before the Lord. Not manufactured on the way to the meeting. Not borrowed secondhand from someone else's study.

Sit with God first. Then hand out the bread.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is what I give to others something I have first received in God's presence?
2. Am I running on stored-up spiritual capital rather than fresh time with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, let what I offer others come first from time spent with You. Keep me from serving out of an empty basket. Amen.
